title: Delivery guarantees: at-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once

videos.script: A consumer reads ten sales from Kafka. It records five of them. Then the machine loses power. {{power}} When it comes back, the consumer has one question. Where was I? {{where}} Kafka keeps the answer, but only the answer the consumer gave it. If it said ten before the crash, five sales are never recorded. If it said nothing, the five are recorded again. {{answers}} Lost, or twice. Those are the two ordinary outcomes, and they have names. At most once. At least once. {{names}} There is a third name, exactly once, and it is the one everybody asks for. Kafka can give it, inside Kafka. Reading, writing and remembering where you were, all in one transaction. {{inside}} Outside Kafka, it cannot. An email sent is sent. {{outside}} In this lesson you crash consumers on purpose, and count what was lost and what was doubled. Then you build a copy that survives the same crash with nothing lost and nothing twice. {{count}}
